title: CuteAFD v4.0.0 against tpurtell's vLLM fork v0.9.2 on K3.25 and K4, and K4-Core-K6 on CuteAFD v4.0.0
question: Does CuteAFD v4.0.0 change precision, speed, memory and long-output behaviour against v3.0.1 and against tpurtell's vLLM fork v0.9.2 on K3.25 and K4, and how far is each checkpoint, including K4-Core-K6, from BF16?
engines: tpurtell vLLM fork (glm-5.3-flash-ext3-2x-rtx) v0.9.2, image index sha256:ea0430aa
tpurtell CuteAFD v4.0.0, coordinator index sha256:e257bc61
tpurtell CuteAFD v3.0.1 (same-day contrast; digest not stated in this run)
checkpoints: wrldsuksgo2mars/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-K3.25-v1 (vLLM fork; revision not stated in this run)
wrldsuksgo2mars/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-K3.25 Core-FP8 build (CuteAFD; revision not stated in this run)
wrldsuksgo2mars/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-K4-Core-K6 (CuteAFD only; revision not stated in this run)
hardware: 2x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition (300 W); GPU only, experts local, no DGX Spark expert nodes

amendments: A1: K4-Core-K6 Block L, declared before it ran
A2: full-vocabulary P-A and a Block L repeat (r2), declared before they ran
